Subject: Question on renewal forecast and potential holdback

Hi Chloe,

Hope you're well — our renewal for Redwood is up in mid-Jan and I wanted to flag a worrying usage dip we saw in Q3 that changed our internal forecast. Attached is a quick usage export and summary (BrightByte_Renewal_Usage_Q3.xlsx). - Can Redwood provide an ARR-exposure view for BrightByte with the current committed SKU mapping?
- Can we get a short list of recommended mitigations (pilot extension, credits, targeted enablement)?
- Is there any flexibility on billing cadence or a staged renewal approach while we validate usage?

We'd like a meeting next week (Dec 6/7) to lock a mutual action plan — procurement is copied.

Thanks,
Jamie Park

Chloe / team — adding my quick read.

Thanks for flagging. From a commercial standpoint I recommend we prepare three discrete options for BrightByte (conservative -> moderate -> proactive):
- Conservative: standard renewal date, 30-day credit tied to Q3 delta, no contract changes.
- Moderate: staged renewal (50% renewed now, 50% POC-linked), 6-month pilot extension, minor SOW amendment.
- Proactive: early renewal with 10% ARR credit + 90-day technical QBR + success metrics.

Naomi — can you run the ARR-exposure table in the attached forecast_snapshot.csv and call out the accounts where usage loss maps to >15% ARR risk? Ben — can you add quick notes on which product modules show the biggest change so we can tailor mitigations?

We should keep the meeting with BrightByte focused (30–45 min) and bring a single recommended option and the rationale.

On internal timing, if we have numbers by EOD Thu (Dec 3) we can circulate a one-page recommendation before the Dec 7 slot.

—Lauren

All — I ran the numbers and summarized below (pulled from the forecast_snapshot.csv). Quick highlights:

- Current committed ARR: $1.6M
- Q3 observed revenue-at-risk (usage dip correlated): ~$210k (~13% of ARR)
- 6 accounts/segments drive 80% of the delta; two large seats are on auto-scaling tiers (likely billing configuration mismatch).

Recommendation:
1) Offer a limited 60-day pilot extension for the affected modules + a $40k one-time credit if usage reattains baseline by end of pilot.
2) If procurement insists on staged renewal, propose a 60/40 split with pro-rated billing and strict SLAs for visibility.
3) If customer accepts proactive early renewal, we can lock a 7% uplift on multi-year commit instead of a pure discount — preserves ARR visibility.

I've also started a billing exception worksheet and attached an SLA-exception-request.pdf for legal/finance review. Sergio — can you weigh in on whether the credit structure is approvable under current fin-ops policy or whether we need an exec sign-off? I can also prepare a short amendment for DocuSign (link below) so we can move quickly if BrightByte signs up.

DocuSign draft: https://app.redwood.com/docusign/AA-987654

—Naomi
